A state in which both writes occur, or in which the compact ledger records an acceptance the source record does not, SHALL NOT be reachable."
whatWasWrong.stateAtBase: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts at b46433b1f computed the reduced market at :294-312 and wrote it ONLY into the journal's `sourcePrivate` envelope. transactionPlacement.mechanism: src/lib/events/journal/SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:98-137 `appendPreparedWithExtension`. Read in this session. `this.db.transaction(() => { ... }).immediate()` at :112-136 wraps BOTH hooks. `prepare(this.db)` runs at :114 and is contractually read-only (:84-97 header). `extend(this.db, prepared.context, () => this.appendInTransaction(...))` runs at :130-132 — it receives the SAME handle and an `append` THUNK, so the caller chooses when the append happens and what runs after it, still inside the one immediate transaction.
transactionPlacement.whereTheRowWriteLands: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts:457 `const appended = append();` then, after the three refusal arms, the `UPDATE campaigns SET payload = ?, version = ? WHERE id = ?` at :481 — inside `extend`, on the `db` handle the writer passed, after the append has reported `committed`. It is therefore part of the SAME command commit, not a second writer path: there is one `.immediate()` transaction and one caller.
transactionPlacement.prepareStaysReadOnly: The next row payload is COMPUTED in `prepare` (`nextSourceRecordAfterAccept` at :252, called at :428 into the context) and APPLIED in `extend`. `prepare` performs no write, honoring the :84-97 contract; the `IPreparedAcceptContext` at :303 is what carries the computed payload across.
transactionPlacement.atomicityConsequence: Every pre-append refusal (`source-record-absent`, `offer-absent`, a rules rejection) returns from `prepare` before `append` is ever called, so the row cannot move for a command that did not commit. A failed append (revision conflict / identity conflict / rejected batch) returns from `extend` BEFORE reaching :481. Pinned by red-first test (b).

observationsForTheNextSlice: Retry vocabulary changed for AcceptContract. An identical re-submit by the same actor used to answer `{kind:'duplicate'}` (the events' sequences differ on the retry, so the command digest differs and the identity arm fires); it now answers `{kind:'offer-not-durable', reason:'offer-absent'}`, because `prepare` reads the reduced market before the append can consult the command log. Both mean "nothing more was written", but 6.2b's client routing must not read `offer-absent` as a retryable durability fact in this case — the offer is gone because THIS actor already consumed it. Pinned by test (e).

The co-op host remains a second ungated AcceptContract writer (recorded, unchanged, in the 6.2b brief's `coopHostSecondWriter`). It does not go through `/api/campaigns/[id]/commands` and therefore neither reduces the row's market nor gains a mission from this write. 6.2b's exactly-once obligation is still only satisfiable for the /commands path until that host path is brought under it or explicitly excluded.

`readCampaignSourceMarket` now refuses a body whose `missions` is malformed even though the pre-6.2a-3 command never read that field. That is a deliberate widening of `source-record-absent`: the row write indexes every mission entry's key, so a body that cannot answer "which mission is this" must be refused rather than rewritten.

RE_1.title: The row write bypassed D2's source-mutation gate.
RE_1.fix: `storedRecordIsNotSource` in campaignAcceptContractCommand.ts, called from `readCampaignSourceMarket` immediately after the stored record and body parse. It runs `parseCampaignAuthority(storedRecord.authority)` and refuses (returns null → the existing typed `source-record-absent`) only when the parse SUCCEEDS and `isSourceInstance` is false.
RE_1.tolerance: `parsed-and-not-source`, never `not-parsed-as-source`, exactly as the review required. A record predating D2 carries no `authority`, `parseCampaignAuthority` answers `failed` for it, and every such row stays acceptable — including every row the existing suites seed. The rationale is recorded in the function's doc comment: `saveCampaign` can afford the stricter reading because it re-stamps the authority it writes, whereas this command only reads and declines to invent a verdict about a record that never claimed one.
RE_1.testRow: (f) refuses a stored record whose authority parses as a replica, appending nothing — seeds `{role:'replica', sourceInstanceId:'src-1', grantId:'grant-1', scopes:['campaign']}` at the envelope level via a new `recordExtras` parameter on the test's `seedSourceRecord`, then asserts the typed `source-record-absent`, a null command receipt, and a byte-identical row.
RE_1.red: MEASURED. Before the guard this row returned `{kind:'committed'}` — the acceptance committed AND the replica's row was rewritten. Captured in red-review-edits.log.

RE_2.title: An offer that is an object but not a usable contract was either an untyped throw or a malformed mission written into the source record.
RE_2.fix: `isStoredContractOffer`, applied to the RAW stored offer at the lookup in `prepare`. It requires `isContract(offer)` AND that `paymentTerms` carries a numeric `salvagePercent` plus six amount fields `rehydrateMoney` reads as amounts.
RE_2.whyIsContractAlone_isNotEnough: MEASURED, and this is the part that goes beyond the review's literal minimal fix. `isContract` accepts any non-null `paymentTerms` object (src/types/campaign/Mission.ts:384-396), so the review's own P2 case — `paymentTerms: {}` — PASSES it. Gating on `isContract` alone would have closed P1 and left P2 exactly as the review found it: rehydration turns the missing amounts into `Money.ZERO`, and the raw offer is copied verbatim into the row, so the campaign records a contract worth nothing as one it signed. The amount check is what actually closes P2.
RE_2.whyNotNarrowerThanRehydrateMoney: `isStoredMoney` mirrors `rehydrateMoney`'s accepted shapes (number, or an object with numeric `amount` or `centsValue`; missionSerialization.ts:19-27) rather than narrowing to the `number` `Money.toJSON` emits. Narrowing would refuse a legacy row that the codebase can already read correctly, which is a different bug from the one being fixed.
RE_2.refusalKindChosen: `offer-absent`, for BOTH halves, and the reason is recorded at the call site. The record and its market read fine — rows (c)/(c2)/(c3) own the case where they do not — and only this one entry fails to be an offer. `source-record-absent` would send an operator to investigate a perfectly readable record, while `offer-absent` names what is true and points at the recovery that can work: get a usable offer to the source, then retry. The `CampaignOfferDurabilityReason` doc comments were updated so the two reasons still describe what they now mean.
testRows: (g) refuses an offer that is an object but not a contract — `offers: [{id: STORED_ID}]`. RED reproduced the review's P1 verbatim: `EventJournalCanonicalizationError: JCS cannot represent undefined`, untyped, out of the prepared transaction.

(h) refuses a contract-shaped offer whose payment terms are unreadable — the real fixture offer with `paymentTerms: {}`. RED reproduced the review's P2: `{kind:'committed'}`, with the offer materialized into the row.
RE_2.bothNowAssert: the typed `offer-absent`, a null command receipt, and a byte-identical `campaigns` row.

a1SizeAccepted.decision: Coordinator, fourth round: row (b) restored into A1 because the write and its atomicity pin belong in one commit, and A1 accepted at its measured size.
a1SizeAccepted.measured: A1 is 645 changed lines (631 insertions + 14 deletions) against a 500-line budget - over by 145. With row (b) in A2 instead it measured 596; that variant was built and discarded by this decision.
a1SizeAccepted.arithmetic: A1's NON-ROW content is 540 changed lines and is the floor for any green commit that carries the product change: the product file 271 (258 + 13), the campaignCommandPipelineArtifactUse fixture completion 20 (19 + 1), and the test file's header, imports, offer fixture, beforeEach/afterEach and seed helpers 249 (lines 1-248 plus the closing brace). 540 > 500 with ZERO test rows present. Rows (a) and (b) add 105 lines on top, giving 645.
a1SizeAccepted.whyTheHarnessCannotMoveOut: Splitting the harness into its own commit would produce a commit whose only new file is a test file containing no `it` blocks. Jest fails such a file ('Your test suite must contain at least one test'), so that commit would not be green on its own - the property this split exists to preserve. 500 is therefore unreachable without weakening the proof.
a1SizeAccepted.whatTheSplitAchieved: Worst commit 798 -> 645 (-19%); two of the three commits are well inside the budget (153 and 57); the product change lands with exactly the two rows that prove it, and the seven remaining refusal rows are reviewable in two test-only steps.
a1SizeAccepted.notDone: No row was trimmed, no test weakened, and no guard dropped to fit the budget.
